toegepas.voor: wat sandbanke en rotse net onder die water wys.
toegepas.na: wat sandbanke en rotse wys wat net onder die water lê.
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written 'net' can be read as 'only' (shows them only under water); placing it with 'lê' makes it clearly 'just below the surface'.
toegepas.fout: 'net onder die water wys' can be read as 'shows them only under the water' instead of 'just below the surface'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting 'net' with 'lê' removes a real ambiguity and adds no new fact.

toegepas.blok: Kies wat by die vraag pas
toegepas.voor: want hulle is op daardie plek gevind
toegepas.na: want die stukke is op daardie plek gevind
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'hulle' sits right after 'die matrose se briewe' and can be read as referring to the letters; naming the pieces removes the ambiguity.
toegepas.fout: 'hulle' follows 'die matrose se briewe' directly and could point to the letters rather than the pieces.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the pieces fixes a pronoun that could point to two things, and the meaning stays the same.

toegepas.voor: wat los van mekaar begin en tog
toegepas.na: wat los van mekaar ontstaan en tog
toegepas.rede_vinder: Sources do not 'begin'; 'ontstaan' is the natural verb for where a clue comes from independently.
toegepas.fout: 'begin' is a loose verb for where a clue comes from.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'ontstaan' is the more exact natural verb for an independent origin and keeps the meaning.

toegepas.voor: want 'n nuwe leidraad kan hom verander.
toegepas.na: want 'n nuwe leidraad kan dit verander.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'dit' is the standard written pronoun for an abstract noun like 'gevolgtrekking' and matches the glossary entry, which already says 'kan dit verander'.
toegepas.fout: 'hom' for the abstract noun 'gevolgtrekking' reads less well in written text than 'dit'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'dit' is the standard pronoun here and makes the sentence match the glossary entry's own 'kan dit verander'.

laat_vaar.voor: Stel jou voor mense kry ou goed in die Kaap se sand.
laat_vaar.na: Stel jou voor dat mense ou goed in die Kaap se sand kry.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Written Afrikaans links 'stel jou voor' to its clause with 'dat' and verb-final order; the spoken run-on reads loosely.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Stel jou voor mense kry...' is natural spoken Afrikaans that suits a Grade 4 reader, so adding 'dat' with verb-final order is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.blok: Kies wat by die vraag pas
laat_vaar.na: Van die leidrade wat wel by die vraag pas,
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'wat pas' hangs without saying what they fit; the heading's own phrase makes the contrast with the set-aside letter clear.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The heading and the sentence before it already say what the clues fit, so the addition only makes an already long sentence longer.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: Asked explicitly: I think it is acceptable Afrikaans for a nine-year-old. It is a regular, transparent noun-plus-noun compound built like 'inligtingsbron' or 'kragbron', needs no linking -s, and both parts are words a Grade 4 learner knows, so its meaning can be read off the word itself. It is probably not in a dictionary, but Afrikaans forms compounds freely and that does not make it wrong. I propose no change; if a different form is ever chosen it must go through all three lessons and the agreed-wordings list, as the entry says.
